source.title: Same Error, Different Function: The Optimizer as an Implicit Prior in Financial Time Series
source.authors: Federico Vittorio Cortesi; G. Iannone; Giulia Crippa; Tomaso A. Poggio; Pierfrancesco Beneventano

record.tranche_reason: Extends optimizer comparisons to daily S&P 500 volatility forecasting, a financial time-series setting. It measures held-out error across architectures and optimizers, but does not test the random-label, width, convolution-versus-fully-connected, dropout, sharpness, or memorized-example claims.
record.gate_note: The study reports held-out NMSE for 12 architecture–optimizer configurations (Table 1). Other results on prediction distances, attributions, portfolios, and curvature do not measure the versions’ specified effects, so they are not catalog rows.
record.test_reason: The study compares optimizers on financial volatility regression after tuning learning rate and weight decay. V4 concerns image-classification and language benchmarks under specified tuning conditions. The study neither measures that limited-tuning effect nor compares limited with broader tuning to establish its removal. Its financial forecasting results therefore fit none of the supplied versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: comparable forecasting errors can conceal optimizer-dependent functions and downstream turnover. Qualify the broad tie: 59 of 66 equality tests do not reject after correction, while positive equivalence evidence depends on exploratory margins. The study does not compare tuned and untuned cohorts to demonstrate that tuning changed or preserved a pre-existing tie.
record.recipe_differences: Financial volatility forecasting rather than the image-classification and language tasks described in V4; four architectures, three optimizers (including Muon), and validation tuning of learning rate and weight decay.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture and optimizer configuration affect reported test NMSE; the authors state the extent of predictive equivalence depends on the chosen tolerance. They report heterogeneous outcomes by architecture and optimizer.

fits_no_version.finding: After validation tuning, Adam has lower mean test NMSE than SGD in all four financial forecasting architectures. No comparison involving SGD rejects equal mean NMSE after Holm correction; this nonrejection does not establish equivalence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Tuned optimizers can have statistically unresolved forecasting-error differences in low-signal financial regression, with substantial architecture-dependent variability across fits.

fits_no_version.finding: The complete financial forecasting grid has seven corrected rejections among 66 comparisons; equivalence counts depend on the exploratory tolerance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Forecasting-error equivalence among architecture–optimizer configurations depends on the comparison and the chosen practical tolerance.

fits_no_version.finding: Comparable forecasting errors coexist with different predictions, lag attributions, and portfolio turnover.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer configurations can select functionally and economically distinct financial predictors despite comparable aggregate held-out error.

record.problems: The paper describes a single financial forecasting task and notes its low signal-to-noise setting. Test NMSE seed uncertainty is reported as SD over 13 runs; the paper cautions that these intervals describe variability conditional on observed data, not uncertainty across financial histories. TOST margins are exploratory and not jointly corrected across margins.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out from the reported 12 configuration-level test NMSE results. Prediction-distance, SHAP, portfolio, and curvature results are omitted because they do not measure the effects named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: Fixed random-label fitting and natural-versus-random-label held-out accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Image-classification comparisons of convolutional and fully connected networks, including local connectivity and initialization effects.
Adaptive-versus-SGD generalization on image and language benchmarks under limited tuning; changes from broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, or optimizer switching.
Large-batch held-out penalties in image classifiers or language models and their recovery through adapted recipes. Financial checkpoint continuations do not establish this effect.
Controlled dropout effects on classifier test error.
Magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation tolerance versus generalization gaps and competing measures. Raw Hessian and directional-curvature diagnostics do not measure this.
Retraining after removing memorized examples versus matched random removals.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the V4 limits_scope verdict: an untested domain and tuning condition are not evidence limiting that version. All twelve extracted NMSE means and SDs match Table 1. Their cannot_determine states concern the supplied versions, not unreadable measurements.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Image-classification and language benchmarks; limited-tuning comparisons and broader tuning conditions in those domains; switching from Adam to SGD and decoupled weight decay.
Large-batch effects under a fixed epoch budget and adaptive training recipes.
Dropout effects and removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness comparisons against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Financial volatility forecasting; validation-selected learning rates and weight decay; 13 runs per architecture–optimizer configuration
reader_labels.reason: In this new domain, the authors report that optimizer-specific tuning leaves performance statistically indistinguishable in most comparisons; the version’s image and language claims are untested (R1–R12).
